title: A Silence for the Postcards
premise: Emrys Fairweather, once a celebrated piano prodigy who vanished from the conservatory's stage at nineteen, has spent fifteen years invisible within its walls as a janitor, cataloguing silences the way she once memorized scores. When the crumbling house where her found family—the eccentric quartet of musicians who raised her—goes up for auction and demolition, she must return to its rooms and confront the question they all arranged their lives around: what really happened the night she stopped playing. As auction day closes in, each member of the household offers a different version of that night, forcing Emrys to choose between protecting their loyalty to one another and claiming the truth of her own broken memory. In the end, she buys back nothing but the truth itself—speaking it aloud in the empty ballroom—and walks out with her family intact for the first time because it is honest rather than silent.
about_author: Tamsin Vane is a former conservatory archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unpublished letters before turning to fiction. She writes about institutions, inheritance, and the people who sweep up after genius.

chapters.title: The Inventory of Unsaid Things
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. Working nights as a janitor in the conservatory where she was once a prodigy, Emrys maintains her mental catalogue of everything unsaid between her and the four musicians who raised her. A legal notice arrives: the childhood house is auctioned, demolition set for spring. The beat is quiet dread—the past has a deadline now.

chapters.title: Four Versions of One Night
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. She visits each former guardian—her old teacher, the cellist, the twins—to ask about the night she stopped playing, and receives four irreconcilable accounts, each lovingly protective and each a lie. Rising tension: she realizes the family's loyalty was built on a shared fiction, and she was its willing centerpiece.

chapters.title: What the Ballroom Kept
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. Breaking into the condemned house the night before the auction, she finds her teacher waiting there, and in the emptied ballroom the true memory surfaces: she didn't fail—she refused to compete against the teacher's own disgraced daughter, and everyone conspired to call it collapse. Climax: grief, accusation, and the first honest sentence spoken in that room in fifteen years.

chapters.title: A Silence, Properly Used
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. At the auction she bids nothing; instead she reads aloud the letter she never sent, releasing the family from the fiction. The guardians, stripped of their arrangement, choose her anyway—not as prodigy or patient but as kin. Resolution: demolition begins behind them as they leave together, silence finally a choice rather than a wall.
